result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.group_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Calculate the betweenness centrality of a group of nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.group_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Calculate the betweenness centrality of a group of nodes. title: >- [Graph.group_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Calculate the betweenness centrality of a group of nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the betweenness centrality of a group of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47793-L47880){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.group_betweenness_centrality( group, normalized=True, endpoints=False, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Group betweenness centrality](/assets/graphs/group-betweenness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph twice. Left, the group C, F intercepts 0.6 of the shortest-path traffic between the five outside nodes, including every path from the triangles to the pendant G. Right, the group A, B sits at the end of the strip, no shortest path between other nodes needs it, and it scores 0.0." width="100%"} Group betweenness (Everett & Borgatti, 1999) measures how much a *set* of nodes, taken together, sits between everyone else: for each pair of nodes outside the group, it adds the fraction of their shortest paths that pass through at least one group member. A path through two members counts once, so the score is not the sum of individual betweenness values, and choosing members that cover *different* routes matters more than choosing the individually most central nodes. Typical uses are picking a team of brokers, monitoring points or checkpoints that together intercept the most traffic. "Shortest" follows `shortest_path()`: hops on an unweighted graph, total weight on a weighted one. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [group]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group's nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `(n - c)(n - c - 1)`, the number of ordered pairs outside a group of size `c`, or by `n(n - 1)`, the number of all ordered pairs, when `endpoints=True`. Either way the score lies in `[0, 1]`. If `False`, return the raw sum (each unordered pair counted once on undirected graphs). [endpoints]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, also count pairs with an endpoint in the group (every such path touches the group). The normalized score is then at least `c(c - 1) / (n(n - 1))`, the share of pairs inside the group. Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure path length by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group betweenness. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the group is empty, contains a node that does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two triangles joined by a bridge C-D, the pair of bridge ends intercepts every path between the triangles, while two nodes from the same triangle intercept far less: ::: {#470de2a2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) ( round(graph.group_betweenness_centrality(["C", "D"]), 3), round(graph.group_betweenness_centrality(["A", "B"]), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.667, 0.0) ``` ::: ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Before version 3.7, NetworkX's `group_betweenness_centrality()` could return values that disagree with this definition (on directed graphs that are not strongly connected, where it could also fail, and on some connected undirected graphs). EdgeCase counts shortest paths directly and agrees with a brute-force count over all of them, as NetworkX 3.7 does. Version 3.7 also changed the `endpoints=True` normalization from `(n - c)(n - c - 1)` to `n(n - 1)`, which EdgeCase follows. `prominent_group()` keeps `(n - k)(n - k - 1)` in both libraries.
